name: bowl_benchmark
comment: The single machine-readable definition of the bowl benchmark. Read by the Python 2.5D prototype, by the Godot true-3D prototype and by the analysis. Neither implementation may hold a copy of any number in here.

units.frame: y up, x and z horizontal, gravity along -y, bowl centred on the y axis with the drain plane at y = 0

bowl.profile_comment: profile_power 1.9 is the shape godot/scripts/neon_scene.gd already draws the production bowl with, and the sweep says it is also the right benchmark. A true paraboloid, power exactly 2.0, is very nearly a harmonic oscillator: every orbit has the same period whatever its amplitude, so eight marbles never lap each other and the run records 48 collisions instead of 166. Off the isochronous point the periods depend on energy, the field mixes, and the benchmark actually exercises the collision handling it is supposed to compare.
bowl.comment: rim_depth and profile_power describe the CENTRE surface - the surface a marble's centre travels on. The collider a 3D engine needs is that surface offset by one marble radius along its inward normal, so the two prototypes constrain the same points.

marble.friction_comment: friction is marble on marble. surface_friction is marble on bowl and is a different pair of materials, so it is a different number - and it has to clear (2/7) tan(theta) at the steepest wall, 0.230 here, or a rigid-body marble cannot roll and skids instead. 0.50 clears it with margin. The 2.5D model assumes rolling and never uses it.

contact.comment: linear_damping is the calibrated dissipation both engines share; see EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md section 5.3. 0.25 was chosen by the sweep in docs/physics_lab_bowl_comparison.md: 0.10 drains nothing inside the limit, 0.15 takes 28.4 s of a 30 s budget, 0.40 empties the bowl in 11 s but costs half the collisions and three of the eight revolutions. rolling_resistance is the physically nicer model and is only used by the 2.5D sweep. rolling_inertia_factor 0.4 is 2/5, a solid sphere.

entry.comment: Eight marbles placed on the bowl wall, evenly spaced in angle with a seeded jitter, at seeded radii, each given a prograde tangential velocity as a seeded fraction of the local circular-orbit speed plus a modest inward radial component. Nothing is dropped at the drain.

calibration.comment: Section 5.3: the two engines are matched on what they DO, not on what they are told. tools/physics_lab_calibrate.py launches one marble into the bowl with no collisions and measures the time for its mechanical energy above the drain lip to halve. PyBullet has a dissipation FLOOR it cannot go below - a sphere loses energy at every triangle edge it rolls over - so it sets the target and the 2.5D damping is bisected to match it. The benchmark's own 0.25/s is what the sweep wanted and is simply not reachable in a rigid-body engine on a tessellated bowl.
